title: yupana: code-fact freshness tracked but unserved; CLAUDE.md claim incomplete
description: yupana watch/overlay_refresh.rs maintains real Recomputing-to-Fresh transitions but freshness_handle/freshness_of have zero production callers outside the module; no query surface serves code-fact freshness (correctly omitted, per FR-3). CLAUDE.md's 'freshness half is Phase 3, not yet served' is incomplete: the verdict surface serves PROJECTION freshness (src/hook/rule_planes.rs:546-566, src/verdict.rs:129). Distinguish code-fact vs projection freshness in docs; wire tracked freshness into query responses at Phase 3.
notes:
PARTIALLY VERIFIED 2026-08-17 (Claude) — deliberately NOT closed, unlike the other six yupana beads re-verified this pass. This bead has two asks and they are in different states. DONE: 'distinguish code-fact vs projection freshness in docs'. yupana CLAUDE.md now says it explicitly — FR-3's freshness half splits in two, code-fact freshness is tracked by src/watch/overlay_refresh.rs but not served, while the verdict surface already serves PROJECTION freshness (src/hook/rule_planes.rs, src/verdict.rs), and 'don't mistake one for the other'. That was the bead's actionable-now half and it is resolved. NOT DONE: 'wire tracked freshness into query responses at Phase 3'. freshness_of has gained a production caller (src/daemon/mod.rs:130, tested at src/daemon/http_test.rs:491-521) so it is reachable, but a query response still omits the tag rather than faking 'fresh' — which yupana's CLAUDE.md states is the correct behaviour until Phase 3 wires it through. So this stays open: the remaining clause is scheduled, not overdue, and closing it would delete the only tracker entry for Phase 3 serving work. Whoever starts Phase 3 should either finish this or split the remainder into its own bead.

RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-17 (Claude), still correctly open — no change to the assessment, recorded so the next pass does not re-derive it. The doc half remains done (yupana CLAUDE.md distinguishes code-fact freshness from projection freshness explicitly). The remaining clause — 'wire tracked freshness into query responses at Phase 3' — is unchanged and should stay unactioned, because yupana's own CLAUDE.md states that a query response omitting the tag rather than faking a 'fresh' one IS the correct behaviour until Phase 3 wires it through. Implementing it now would contradict that repo's documented phasing, which is a keeper decision and not a bobbin-side one.

Left open deliberately rather than closed: this is the only tracker entry for Phase 3 serving work, and closing it would delete that. Reviewed alongside the other bobbin beads this pass; it is scheduled, not stale.
close_reason:
Both clauses now done. The doc half was already resolved; the remaining clause — 'wire tracked freshness into query responses at Phase 3' — is implemented in yupana this pass.

WHY IT WAS UNSERVED, precisely: the tracking lives on the daemon's ResidentEngine (freshness_of, src/daemon/mod.rs:130) and the MCP server holds no engine handle — it reads files and extracts symbols on demand. The seam that DOES have the engine is the daemon's /symbols handler, which is where this landed.

Implemented: FileSymbols gains an optional freshness field, populated on the tenant-scoped path from the tracker, read BEFORE the view is composed so the tag describes the state the returned symbols came from rather than one that moved underneath the read.

THE OMIT RULE SURVIVES THE WIRING RATHER THAN BEING REPLACED BY IT, and that is the part I would defend. Freshness is absent when the tenant never had an edit absorbed, and absent on the untenanted path, which has no tenant to key the map by. Never 'fresh', never 'unknown', never a default — a fabricated tag is indistinguishable from a measured one, which is the entire reason the tag exists. serde skip_serializing_if so it is genuinely absent from the JSON rather than null.

Pinned by symbols_serve_code_fact_freshness_and_omit_it_when_unknown, covering all four cases (served after an absorbed edit; omitted before one; per-tenant, so tenant b gets nothing; omitted on the untenanted surface). PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL: defaulting an unknown freshness to 'fresh' turns it red on the omit assertion with the actual JSON in the message.

yupana CLAUDE.md updated. The old text said code-fact freshness is 'tracked but not yet served — omits rather than faking until Phase 3'; it now says served on the tenant-scoped reply, still omitted where unknown, and that projection freshness remains a different quantity that can disagree. Both halves of the distinction the bead was originally about are now correct in the docs.

387 tests pass with --features mcp; clippy clean under -D warnings; docs lint clean. Committed in yupana on the same branch.

title: paper: establish which ablation arms are valid — measurements predate two bug fixes
description: The context-injection paper draft (docs/paper-context-injection.md) is dated 2026-03-05. Two bugs in mechanisms it ablates were fixed 2026-08-17, five months later: cee3cdc (complementary expansion kept non-adjacent duplicates, so one file could consume several of the five truncated slots) and 7d99f03 (intent doc-demotion factor inverted on the local hook path — a 1.5 factor that strengthened demotion remotely weakened it locally). The 66-run and 85-run measurements were therefore taken against code where at least two mechanisms did not behave as the paper describes them. Determine per-arm which numbers survive. Complementary expansion and coupling expansion are distinct mechanisms, so the reported -0.247 coupling arm may be unaffected; that needs checking rather than assuming. Outcome is either a re-run of the affected arms or an explicit statement that all numbers are against a pinned pre-fix commit, with the divergence named. Do not draft around these numbers until this is settled.
acceptance_criteria: Each reported figure is either re-measured post-fix, or attributed to a named commit with the behavioural divergence stated in the paper.
close_reason:
Settled: NEITHER fix affects any arm, and no re-run is needed on their account. Full per-arm verdict table in docs/plans/paper-measurement-validity.md.

cee3cdc (complementary expansion) is UNREACHABLE under the eval harness. The branch requires reducing_enabled && reduced_count > 0 — i.e. a second or later UserPromptSubmit, once the SessionLedger holds entries from a previous turn. eval/runner/agent_runner.py runs 'claude -p <prompt>': exactly one UserPromptSubmit per run. Confirmed empirically — every run's *_metrics.jsonl records exactly one 'hook inject-context' event.

Coupling expansion confirmed DISTINCT, as the bead asked rather than assumed: config.git.coupling_depth is an INDEXING parameter (src/cli/index.rs:709) controlling how many commits are mined into the co-change table; complementary expansion is a query-time fallback reading that table via get_coupling(seen_file, 5). Shared data source, nothing else. The -0.247 coupling arm is unaffected.

7d99f03 (doc-demotion inversion) is in code that DID NOT EXIST at measurement time. Proof from run artifacts, not inference: ruff-003/004/005 classify as Operational under today's classifier, and today's inject-context returns early WITHOUT injecting for Operational — yet those three runs record chunks_returned of 20, 20 and 19. The Operational skip and the intent-adjustment path where the lpp bug lived were added together, so neither was in the measured binary. (This repo's git history begins 2026-07-24 and does not reach the measurement dates, so it had to be established from artifacts.)

Pinned by src/search/eval_prompt_intent_tests.rs, which fixes each task's intent and asserts the boilerplate drives the classification.

The investigation surfaced two LARGER threats the bead did not ask about, both now written into the paper:
(1) The five Flask tasks were quarantined 2026-02-15 for a 0% test pass rate on BOTH arms — broken setup_command/test_command, not a bobbin result — yet the March draft still reported all five, counted them in '13 tasks', built its ENTIRE calibration sweep on them, and read their flat deltas as evidence about Flask's code quality. Flask and the sweep are now withdrawn (paper 4.2, 5.7).
(2) The gate_threshold=1.0 arm injected NOTHING — chunks=None in all three runs, against 17-20 elsewhere — because threshold 1.0 means the bar can never be cleared. It is a third baseline, not an ablation. Comparing it against both baselines attributes ~92% of the headline effect to tool availability rather than to injection (paper 5.2). That is the study's most consequential number and it was hiding in a mislabelled arm.

title: paper: lead with the ablation, not the aggregate improvement
description: The draft's headline is F1 0.695 -> 0.722 and duration 252s -> 209s. That is +0.027 F1 across 66 runs and it will not survive review as a primary claim; a reviewer asks for significance and gets an uncomfortable answer. The strong result is the decomposition, where the effects are large and unambiguous: semantic search -0.384 when disabled, git blame bridging -0.303, temporal coupling expansion -0.247. Restructure so the contribution is 'which of six injection methods actually carries the weight, measured by removal' rather than 'injection helps'. The aggregate improvement becomes a supporting number, not the thesis. This is the same editorial move that fixed the yupana paper plan: the decomposition is the result, the margin is not.
acceptance_criteria: Abstract and introduction lead with the ablation decomposition; the aggregate delta appears as support, not as the headline.
close_reason:
Done. Paper restructured so the decomposition is the thesis; the aggregate is demoted to supporting context. Retitled 'Decomposing Context Injection for AI Coding Agents'. New 1.1 makes the case explicitly: removal effects run up to 0.384 F1 against an aggregate of 0.027, and 'injection helps' is already the premise of every system in the space, so the open question is which composed method carries the weight. Results reordered — 5.1 ablation, 5.2 the confound, 5.3 power, and only then 5.4 aggregate. Conclusion and abstract rewritten to match.

One correction to the bead's premise, which changes the framing but not the direction. The bead says to lead with the decomposition because 'the effects are large and unambiguous'. They are large; they are NOT unambiguous — see bobbin-55: after Holm correction across six arms, nothing is significant, and five of six intervals cross zero. So the reframe landed as 'a method for decomposing injection systems, demonstrated on a pilot, with a ranking whose grouping is the transferable result' rather than as settled magnitudes. That version survives review; 'semantic search contributes -0.384' as a bare claim does not.

The grouping IS robust in the sense that matters: retrieval-expansion (0.247-0.384) separates from filtering (0.025-0.080) by an order of magnitude, and that separation does not depend on any individual arm reaching significance.

title: paper: significance testing and power for the thin ablation conditions
description: The draft's own abstract concedes 'small sample sizes for several ablation conditions'. Conceding it is not the same as quantifying it. Add confidence intervals or appropriate tests to every reported ablation effect, and name explicitly which conditions are underpowered rather than leaving the reader to infer it from run counts. If an arm cannot support a claim, say so and drop the claim — an ablation table with three solid rows and an honest gap is stronger than six rows of which half are noise. Pairs with the reframe bead: if the ablation is the thesis, its statistics carry the paper.
acceptance_criteria: Every ablation effect reports an interval or test; underpowered conditions are named in the results section, not only in the discussion.
close_reason:
Done. Welch's t-test (mandatory — arm SDs span 0.000 to 0.385), 95% CIs on every arm, Holm-Bonferroni across the six comparisons, and a power analysis. Written into paper 5.3, detailed in docs/plans/paper-statistics.md, regenerated by scripts/paper_stats.py.

The answer is worse than 'several conditions are thin'. Five of six confidence intervals cross zero. AFTER CORRECTION, NO ARM IS SIGNIFICANT — the one nominally significant result (semantic_weight=0.0, p=0.030) misses its corrected threshold of 0.0083 by nearly fourfold. Correction is mandatory rather than conservative here: 'which of six methods carries the weight' IS a six-way comparison.

The headline baseline contrast is also not significant: ruff-001 with-bobbin vs no-bobbin is d=+0.312, p=0.055, CI [-0.009, +0.633]. And the 66-run aggregate cannot be tested AT ALL because Table 1 reported means with no SDs — a reporting defect independent of sample size, now flagged in the paper and in Appendix A.

Acted on the bead's instruction to drop unsupportable claims. The three filtering effects (doc demotion, recency, gating) are no longer claimed: their intervals span most of the metric's range, so the study contains essentially no information about them. Power: 14 / 22 / 32 runs per arm would establish the three retrieval-expansion effects at 80% power (~70 runs, ~$105, one day — a fundable follow-up), while the filtering effects would need 297 / 3026 / 3026 and should not be run at all. Stated as lower bounds, since pilots that reach significance overestimate effect size.
notes:
2026-08-18 (strider): the aggregate reporting defect this bead flagged is resolved. scripts/paper_census.py recomputes Table 5 from eval/results/runs/, so it now carries SDs and is testable: reported tasks only, with-bobbin 0.743 +/- 0.270 (N=21) vs no-bobbin 0.671 +/- 0.263 (N=20), delta +0.072, t=0.86, df=39.0, p=0.395, 95% CI [-0.097, +0.240]. Conclusion unchanged (inside the noise); the reason changes from 'cannot be tested' to 'tested, p=0.395'. The recount also verified all ten rows of Table 7 reproduce exactly from artifacts, so sections 5.1-5.3 stand as computed.

2026-08-18 (strider), second finding, more serious than the first: the with-bobbin baseline that every ablation arm is compared against is NOT model-matched. All 19 ablation runs are confirmed claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929; the 7-run baseline is 4 confirmed Sonnet, 1 confirmed claude-opus-4-6 (F1=1.000, tied highest in the arm), 1 declared-Sonnet-unbilled, 1 with no model record. Restricting the baseline to its 4 matched runs (0.530 +/- 0.327 vs published 0.636 +/- 0.347) shrinks every effect, flips the sign of three (doc_demotion +0.026, recency +0.081, gate +0.081), and drops semantic_weight=0.0 from p=0.030 to p=0.191 — it loses nominal significance before any correction. The retrieval/filtering grouping survives and sharpens: the groups now separate by sign, not just magnitude. Written up as paper section 5.1.1 (new Table 2) and docs/plans/paper-statistics.md section 4b. Root cause is a harness defect: 45 of 85 runs record no serving model at all.

title: paper: write the related work section — none exists
description: The draft has no related work at all. Areas to cover: retrieval-augmented generation and hybrid lexical+dense retrieval; rank fusion (RRF is the baseline a reviewer names by default); code search; agent context management and context-window budgeting; repository-history supervision (using commit history as labels is the paper's most unusual move and needs positioning against whatever exists); and Monitor-Guided Decoding, which is the nearest neighbour to injecting analysis facts into a model's loop. Reuse the bibliography assembled for the quipu paper where it overlaps rather than rebuilding it.
acceptance_criteria: A related work section positioning both headline mechanisms — blame-provenance bridging and commit-history-supervised calibration — against named prior work.
close_reason:
Done. Section 7 Related Work written, covering every area the bead named: RAG (Lewis, REALM, Atlas) with the setting difference stated; hybrid lexical+dense and rank fusion, naming RRF (Cormack 2009) explicitly as the baseline a reviewer reaches for and which bobbin in fact uses; code search (CodeSearchNet, CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT) with the point that it optimises against human relevance judgements while this paper measures a downstream behavioural effect — and section 5.6 is a concrete case where the two diverge; agent context management and budgeting (MemGPT, Xu 2024); repository-history supervision positioned against the co-change/defect-prediction literature (Zimmermann 2005), with blame bridging identified as the component with no external precedent we are aware of and therefore the one most needing replication; and Monitor-Guided Decoding (Agrawal 2023) as the nearest neighbour, contrasted on granularity and timing — per-token hard constraint from a type system versus per-turn soft prior from retrieval and history. Added SWE-bench for agent evaluation, which the bead did not list but which a reviewer will expect.

Bibliography reuse noted as the bead instructed: overlap with the quipu references.bib for RAG and agent evaluation; the new entries needed are listed in docs/plans/paper-arxiv-submission.md section 4.

ONE THING DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, flagged rather than faked: the section is prose with author-year references and carries NO citation keys or BibTeX entries. Those entries were written from working knowledge and have NOT been checked against the published record. Verifying every author list, year and venue is a required step before submission and is called out as such in the arXiv plan — a fabricated or misattributed citation is the most damaging and most avoidable error in a submission.

title: paper: move the small-N limitation into the abstract
description: Sample-size limits currently live in the discussion. With 66 runs across 13 tasks and several thin ablation arms, that belongs in the abstract. Stating a limit early is a credibility asset and costs nothing; discovering it late reads as concealment. Same discipline the yupana eval note already follows with its explicit threats-to-validity section.
acceptance_criteria: The abstract states the run counts and the small-sample caveat.
close_reason:
Done. The sample-size limit is now in the abstract, in its own paragraph, stated before any result is elaborated: 3-4 runs per arm, baseline SD 0.347, no arm surviving Holm-Bonferroni across the six comparisons, and the aggregate effect smaller than the noise. The abstract also carries the power figures (14/22/32 to establish the three retrieval-expansion effects; 300-3,000 for the filtering ones) so a reader knows the scale of what is missing, not just that something is.

Went further than the bead asked in one respect, and it was warranted. The bead's rationale is that stating a limit early is a credibility asset while discovering it late reads as concealment. The same argument applies to the tool-availability confound found while working bobbin-53 — one ablation arm turned out to disable injection entirely, and comparing it against both baselines attributes ~92% of the headline effect to tool availability rather than injection. That is a more serious limitation than small N and it is now also in the abstract rather than buried in the discussion. Section 6.3 keeps the full limitations list; the abstract carries the two that change how the whole paper should be read.

The draft is markdown and will need a LaTeX conversion; quipu/docs/paper/ is the working template.

close_reason:
Done. docs/plans/paper-arxiv-submission.md written, following the quipu process (arXiv:submit/7961151) as the bead directed.

Mechanics settled: cs.SE primary with cs.IR and cs.AI cross-list — the reverse of quipu's, correctly, since this is a tooling-and-measurement paper rather than a knowledge-representation argument; cs.IR added because the decomposition is a retrieval-methods ablation. Endorsement is held for cs.AI; cs.SE-as-primary may need its own and should be checked BEFORE filing, with cs.IR primary as the fallback. Licence CC BY 4.0, matching quipu, not the arXiv default. LaTeX conversion planned against quipu/docs/paper/ as template, with this paper's specifics: 1:1 section mapping (the markdown was renumbered for it), eight tables to booktabs, and the Unicode trap — the draft uses ± and U+2212 minus freely and a naive paste will render badly. Recommended one figure: a forest plot of the six effects with their CIs, which communicates 'five of six cross zero' instantly. The External DOI trap is documented as the bead asked: that field is for a published version of the same paper, NOT the Zenodo artifact DOI, which belongs in the author footnote.

Artifact archival extended beyond quipu's shape, because this paper's evidence is bigger: eval/tasks/ INCLUDING _quarantined/ (its README is load-bearing evidence for 4.2), eval/results/runs/ per-run artifacts (section 5.2's claim that one arm injected nothing is checkable only against the *_metrics.jsonl files), and scripts/paper_stats.py.

DO NOT SUBMIT YET, and the plan opens by saying so. The blockers are content, not mechanics: no arm survives correction (bobbin-55), and the tool-availability confound means the paper's central mechanism is confounded by its own data. Recommendation recorded for the keeper: run the missing fourth arm — installed and advertised, hook disabled — at ~30 runs, ~$45, half a day. It is the cheapest thing that changes what the paper can claim, and a reviewer who reads 5.2 will ask for it. Submitting as a methodological/negative result is the defensible alternative but is a materially different paper, and that is ian's call.
notes: 2026-08-18 (strider): order-of-operations steps 2 and 3 are done. Run-count discrepancy resolved by direct recount (scripts/paper_census.py): 85 = whole study, 96 = protocol intent never executed, 108 = unattributable; the ablation is 19 runs. Aggregate dispersion recomputed. The recount also found that the published 66-run Table 5 aggregate included the 25 withdrawn Flask runs and that its test-pass-rate finding (65.5% -> 47.2%) was entirely that contamination, not polars-004 as the draft claimed. Remaining blockers: the keeper decision on the fourth arm (step 1), citation verification (step 4), LaTeX conversion (step 5).

title: Failure and post-tool-use injections lack injection IDs and bypass the session ledger
description: Only prompt-submission paths generate injection identifiers and store injection records (src/cli/hook.rs:1450/1509, 3219/3234-3246); the failure-handler's semantic fallback passes None (hook.rs:4672) and the parse-directed and post-tool-use paths store nothing, so those injections cannot be rated via feedback. They neither filter against nor record to the SessionLedger (hook.rs:1164-1176/1481, 3089-3110/3274-3276), so they can re-inject chunks the prompt path already delivered, invisible to delta filtering. Extend the ID scheme and ledger integration to all injecting event classes. Found by adversarial doc-vs-code review (Claude agent session, 2026-08-14).
close_reason:
Implemented for both injecting event classes the bead names.

New InjectionTurn (src/cli/hook.rs, next to SessionLedger) owns a single non-prompt injecting turn: which chunks are still fresh, which were claimed, and the one injection identifier they are recorded under. One type rather than three copies of the same six lines, because three copies is how these paths diverged from the prompt path to begin with.

PostToolUseFailure — both branches. The parse-directed pass now claims every chunk before rendering it, including the coupled-file previews, so an error file the prompt path already delivered is not sent again. The semantic fallback filters the bundle against the ledger before formatting and bails with a skip message if nothing survives; it previously passed None as the injection id (hook.rs:4672 as filed) and now passes the turn's. Both record an injection through store_injection_with_output, so failure-path injections can be rated through feedback for the first time.

PostToolUse — the related-files listing suggests files rather than injecting chunk bodies, so it claims at file level using the path:0:0 marker convention complementary expansion already writes to this ledger. Coupled and semantic suggestions are both filtered, before the section headers decide whether there is anything left to say. One deliberate asymmetry, tested: a file marker does NOT suppress a later chunk-level injection of that file, because naming a file and showing its contents are different deliveries and the second is still worth making.

Two ordering decisions worth recording. record_non_prompt_injection runs only AFTER the response is on stdout — recording chunks a turn never emitted would suppress them next turn for nothing — and it is best-effort throughout, because a feedback store that will not open must never turn a delivered injection into a failed hook. Both are pinned by tests (an uncommitted turn must leave the ledger untouched).

Within-turn dedup applies even when reducing is disabled: cross-turn filtering is configurable, emitting the same chunk twice in one response never is. A turn with no session id degrades to in-memory dedup but still carries an identifier, so callers never branch on whether Claude Code supplied one.

injection_id and ledger_chunks now appear in the metrics for both handlers, including the post-tool-use skip path.

12 tests in src/cli/hook_injection_turn_tests.rs. Suite 951 passed / 0 failed (was 939); clippy unchanged at 207; file-size gate unchanged at 10 errors / 6 warnings.

NOT COVERED, deliberately: the remote variants (run_post_tool_use_failure_remote) and the prime-context path. The remote paths go through the HTTP client and have no local ledger to consult; giving them ledger semantics is a separate piece of work and a separate bead if wanted.

title: yupana: the fleet's edit guard invokes `hank`, a binary that no longer exists

1. The epic's premise is that a record must answer WHICH PIECE OF WORK caused an action (src/plate.rs:1-9). The `guard` kind — by far the highest-volume record — cannot answer it.
2. docs/work-scoped-governance.md gates advise->enforce promotion on REPLAY over recorded action records ('turns the advise/block decision from a waiting game into a computation'). Replaying a temporal rule needs a session-scoped event stream. Without a session id the records cannot be grouped into sessions, so no windowed rule can be replayed at all.

FIX: add `session` (from HookInput.session_id, already parsed at src/hook/mod.rs:53-55) to every spool line, and `item` to the `guard` kind.

ACCEPTANCE: every emitted line carries session when the harness supplied one and omits it otherwise (never a fabricated value, per the FR-3 omit-don't-fake rule); guard records carry item when the plate resolved one; a test asserts both.
notes: These are also exactly the two fields that would make the spool replayable by an external temporal-policy engine — see the Dogwood/Cedar assessment bead.
close_reason: Done. `session` (from HookInput.session_id) on every spool line and `item` (from the plate) on the guard kind, both OMITTED rather than blanked when unresolved. This is what makes the records replayable rather than merely auditable — a windowed rule had nothing to group by, which is why the advise-to-enforce promotion gate had never been runnable.

title: yupana: an advise-mode scope advisory never reaches the agent it is meant to steer
description:
docs/book/src/reference/policy-guard.md:247-257 records the measurement: at mode = advise the guard reports via `systemMessage`, which surfaces in the operator's pane and DOES NOT enter the model's context. The doc is blunt — 'Only enforce puts the reason in front of the model' — and says it was confirmed by running the same violating edit in both modes on a live pane.

So the whole staged posture is hollow at its first rung: `work_item_scope = advise` produces an advisory nobody who could act on it can see. The doc already draws the right conclusion for measurement ('agents behaved no differently under advise is not evidence that they saw the advisory; they did not') but the containment goal needs more than an uncorrected rate — it needs the agent to learn where its ground ends.

FIX: route the out-of-ground advisory through the PostToolUse `additionalContext` channel, which already exists and already reaches the model (src/hook/post_edit.rs:63-65), rather than systemMessage. Pre-edit keeps its current job — the enforce deny and the once-per-session unknown-scope notice — and stays off the critical path. The Post-Action Auditor (src/hook/paa.rs) is what this is for: it judges completed state and changes what happens next.

ACCEPTANCE: both-outcomes — an edit outside the item's ground produces an additionalContext section naming the item and both legitimate exits; an edit inside the ground produces nothing. scope_arm.rs's Violation is reused rather than reimplemented, so there is exactly one definition of 'outside the ground'.
notes: This is the single most important gap for a containment posture of advise. Without it the posture reaches nobody.
close_reason: Done via src/hook/scope_notice.rs: the out-of-ground advisory now rides PostToolUse additionalContext, which reaches the model, instead of systemMessage, which reaches only the operator's pane. scope_arm keeps the enforce deny and the once-per-session unknown-scope notice; both call Scope::check_path against the same projected WorkItemScopes so there is one definition of 'outside the ground'. Silent when it cannot speak honestly — no plate, no scope, unreachable store, or an edit inside the ground. UNKNOWN IS NOT A DEVIATION.

title: yupana: the work-item briefing is all-or-nothing; make it a disclosure ladder with an honest census
description:
src/brief.rs:144 render() prints every section in full at session start — ground with symbols and callers, central entities, similar past work, related items, rules in force. It is a single push with no way to ask for more and no statement of what was withheld (the 5-item similar-work cap is invisible; docs/briefing-retrieval-eval.md notes it as a measured recall cost).

FIX: split render into L0 + the existing full render. L0 carries item id, label, ground PATHS only, scope posture, and one census line per withheld section naming its size and the call that expands it. The expansions are quipu_ask named queries (see the quipu-side bead), so the handles L0 advertises are real and parameter-validated.

The estate already states the rule this follows: the envelope rule (camayoc docs/patents/provisional-grounding-cluster.md sec 7 — the tier rides the response envelope, so an empty answer still declares the tier at which nothing was found) and typed non-answers (sec 8 — a verdict returns the violation classes it did NOT check, so a pass is a bounded claim). quipu/src/graph_view.rs:239-245 implements the same idea as `truncated: {shown, of}`.

MUST NOT REGRESS the three existing honesty behaviours, each covered by a test: an unprojectable store says 'could not be read, not because nothing governs you'; an empty ground reads as a fresh start, not a wide scope; a cache-served projection states its age.

MUST carry plane/trust attribution: a census line reading '4 similar items' when three are crew:inferred is the masquerade camayoc's plane discipline exists to prevent.

ACCEPTANCE: census counts match what the expansion actually returns; brief.rs stays under the file-size ratchet (it is already 337 lines, warn at 400) so the split lands in a sibling module.
notes: L0 is a strict subset of what render() prints today plus counts — no new retrieval.
close_reason: Done as src/brief_l0.rs. L0 keeps the item, its ground PATHS and the posture, and replaces each remaining section with one line naming its size and the quipu_ask rung that expands it — those rungs shipped in the same push on the quipu side, so the handles are redeemable rather than suggestions. A section with nothing in it prints NO line; a census that always fires trains an agent to skip it. All three honesty behaviours survive with their own tests, and one test asserts L0 is actually smaller than the full render.

title: yupana: page in context about where an agent went, at the moment it leaves its ground
description:
The symmetry docs/work-scoped-governance.md sec 3 names — 'if the graph can predict what an agent may access, it can predict what that agent will need to read, and those are nearly the same query' — is currently only exploited at assignment time. When an agent actually strays, it gets a refusal or nothing, never the context that would have prevented the stray.

FIX: when a landed edit falls outside the item's ground, the PostToolUse advisory (see the advise-channel bead) carries the next disclosure level ABOUT THE PATH JUST TOUCHED: its central entities, which prior work item touched it, and whether that item's outcome was done. Same sources brief_sources.rs already uses (quipu /context, /project pagerank, and the existing entity_work / cochanged_with named queries), seeded on the deviation instead of on the ground.

WHY POST-EDIT AND NOT PRE-EDIT: pre-edit already costs 157-322ms against a 100ms deadline_ms budget, and src/hook/scope_arm.rs:24-32 states the rule that the scope arm never adds a projection round-trip of its own. Post-edit is off the critical path and is the only non-blocking channel that reaches the model.

ACCEPTANCE: recoverability — break the expansion source and the edit still proceeds and the advisory still names the item; the expansion states its own staleness when served from the projection cache.
notes: Depends on the advise-channel bead. This is the piece that makes disclosure PACED by behaviour rather than dumped once.
close_reason: Done. The post-edit notice now carries what the graph knows about the path just touched — which prior work items modified it and how those turned out — via src/brief_deviation.rs. Seeded on the deviation rather than the ground, which is the half of the scope/context symmetry nobody was serving. Affordable only here: the pre-edit path has a 100ms deadline and scope_arm is forbidden a round-trip of its own; post-edit has neither constraint.

title: shantytown: wire yupana's session-start briefing and pre-bash trace; fix the guard binary name
description:
FOLLOW-UP, filed here because yupana has no local bead store and this is yupana-owned work that lands in another repo. shantytown was explicitly out of scope for the change that found this.

Three unwired or misdirected hooks in shantytown/shantytown/runtime.py:

1. runtime.py:446 `_HANK_GUARD` invokes `hank hook pre-edit`; the binary is `yupana`. One-line fix, plus three assertions in shantytown/tests/test_role_emit.py:107,126,155. See the guard-name bead for why this is urgent.
2. runtime.py:614 session_start_hooks() emits ONLY the static query-first directive. `yupana hook session-start` — the fully built, ablation-evaluated (macro-F1 0.954) work-item briefing — is wired by nothing and reaches no agent.
3. runtime.py:677 pre_tool_use_hooks() puts only the deployment's SHANTY_BASH_GUARD on the Bash matcher. `yupana hook pre-bash` is wired by nothing, so the action trace has no input, so no rule can ever earn promotion by replay.

DELIVERY MATTERS: new hooks belong in the consent file (shantytown/shantytown/provision.py:63, settings.local.json), which is re-applied on EVERY launch and self-heals, NOT in --settings, which is written only on `role set` and already went stale fleet-wide once (runtime.py:698-702). Governance that reaches nobody is decoration.

Also dead: st anchor's context= / knowledge= parameters are never passed (shantytown/shantytown/cli.py:2789), so the anchor's CONTEXT (bobbin) and KNOWN (quipu) sections can never render.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18. Each of the three is small; the delivery-path detail is the part that is easy to get wrong.
close_reason: All three legs done. The guard name is fixed at the emitter; `yupana hook session-start` is wired into session_start_hooks beside query_first (complementary, not a replacement); `yupana hook pre-bash` is wired on the Bash matcher and emitted for BOTH harnesses, since the payload shape was already measured identical for codex. One consequence worth recording: both read_bash_guard readers had to learn that a recorder is not a guard, or roles --check would have reported coverage for a deployment that configured none.

title: yupana: the Bash surface is recorded but ungoverned, so scope contains edits only
description:
src/hook/pre_bash.rs is RECORD-ONLY by design and says so: it never denies, never warns, prints nothing, always exits 0. That was correct for the trace phase — enforcement on the action path is gated on evals, and a hook that started advising there would be enforcement arriving without the gate.

But it means work-item scope contains Edit|Write|MultiEdit and nothing else. An agent held to its ground on the edit tools can still reach outside it with `sed -i`, a heredoc, or a script. Phase 3 of docs/work-scoped-governance.md names this: 'extend the matcher surface to tool-call classes currently ungoverned'.

BLOCKED ON: the trace actually having records (see the session/item bead) and a replayed false-positive rate, because promoting a Bash rule without replay evidence is exactly the failure the promotion ladder exists to prevent.

Not to be fixed opportunistically — filed so the limit is visible rather than discovered.
notes: Stated honestly in docs/work-scoped-governance.md's 'What this cannot reach' table too: the guard sees one command string, not the N it triggers.
close_reason: Done, staged off. Scope gains allow_targets/deny_targets matched as class:target against what a command resolves to, with [yupana.policy] action_scope = off|advise|enforce and the ambient mode as ceiling. DECLARED ONLY, and that is about the data rather than a shortcut: nothing in the graph records which hosts an item's prior work touched, so there is no observed rung to build — and declared is the one provenance the trust ladder permits to hard-deny. OFF BY DEFAULT is the contract, not a convenience: pre-bash has been record-only since it shipped, and a hook that started refusing the moment the code landed would be enforcement arriving without its gate. An abstention is never a violation; writing that test found the resolver's discipline working, since 'ssh prod-01' abstains on a bare undotted word.

title: yupana: only the `observed` scope rung exists, so new files always read as deviation
description:
docs/work-scoped-governance.md defines a three-rung ladder — declared (explicit edges on the item, highest trust) > derived (labels, parent epic, structural graph) > observed (what prior sessions actually touched). src/policy.rs:204-218 has the ScopeProvenance enum for all three, and the Derived variant carries a '(No source yet.)' comment. Only observed is live.

Observed scope is what work HAS touched, not what it MAY touch. So a legitimately new file — the common case when an item's first commit has not landed — always falls outside. At advise that is tolerable noise; at enforce it would be an outage, which is why advise is the right ceiling until the upper rungs exist.

NOTE ON VOCABULARY, worth recording before anyone implements: the design doc sketches declared scope as `gov:WorkItem` / `gov:touchesRepo` / `gov:grantsAction`. There is NO `gov:` prefix anywhere in camayoc, quipu, or yupana. Meanwhile aegis:WorkItem already exists, and aegis:appliesTo (src/project_queries.rs:18-26,50) already IS a rule's multi-valued path scope with absent meaning unscoped — the nearest existing declared-scope predicate. Extend aegis: through camayoc's schema process; do not mint a namespace a design doc invented.

WATCH OUT: POLICY_QUERY and GROUNDED_POLICY_QUERY target the SUPERTYPE (?s a/rdfs:subClassOf* aegis:TextRule) so new rule kinds bind automatically — a new scope rule class will be picked up by the running guard whether or not that was intended.
notes: The namespace and supertype notes are the expensive part to rediscover; the rungs themselves are ordinary work.
close_reason: The DERIVED rung shipped: an item with no observed ground of its own inherits its parent's, via aegis:contains — quipu's existing epic/bead hierarchy, so no vocabulary was minted and the gov: namespace stayed unused, as this bead argued. Two rules make it safe and both are tested: an inference must not override a record (evaluated only when the item has no ground of its own), and it never hard-denies at any rung setting, because refusing on a SIBLING's history would strand an agent on somebody else's record. A rung that can answer and finds the edit inside returns Allow rather than falling through to 'UNGUARDED by scope' — saying that about an edit a rung just cleared is false in the direction that gets advisories ignored. The DECLARED rung's graph vocabulary is still design intent; the supertype-projection warning recorded here still applies to whoever builds it.

title: yupana: the plate keeps confidently naming a work item after it closes
description:
src/plate.rs:31-45 documents the window and does not close it: a plate written while an item was open keeps answering after that item closes, so every later action is attributed to the closed item — plausibly, which is the dangerous kind of wrong. Two partial mitigations exist (the publisher rewrites at every resolution point; a 4h max_age backstop refuses a plate left by a dead session) and neither closes it.

The module states the fix: 'closing it wants a session id on both sides, which the harness has and the publisher does not yet carry'. shantytown/shantytown/plate_publish.py already writes a `session` field and its reader already supports a session guard — so the missing half is the publisher consistently supplying it and yupana comparing against HookInput.session_id.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: these records get REPLAYED to derive enforcement rules. A wrong work item does not merely mislabel one action, it manufactures a false justification for a rule that then applies to everyone.

NOTE: this is the same session id the spool needs (see the session/item bead) — one field, three payoffs.
notes: Filed 2026-08-18 while planning containment. Bounded by publisher cadence today, not closed.
close_reason: Closed by fixing the bigger half of the window this bead only half-named. plate_publish.publish had exactly ONE caller — st anchor — so the plate was not merely stale between a close and a republish, it named the agent's PREVIOUS item until the agent happened to anchor, and never updated at all for one that did not. st go now publishes on the success path only, after send, verify and a read-back tracker write; a refused or unverified dispatch publishes nothing, which matters more than the positive case. The module docstring that claimed the publisher 'rewrites the plate at every point it resolves one' was false and is corrected rather than quietly made true. The session-id comparison remains available for the residual close-to-republish window, which is now bounded by dispatch rather than by an agent's habits.

title: yupana: evaluate Dogwood/Cedar as the offline replay harness for rule promotion
description:
ASSESSMENT DONE 2026-08-18; this bead records the conclusion and the one action worth taking.

AWS open-sourced Dogwood on 2026-08-06 (Apache-2.0, Rust: dogwood-language / dogwood-cli). It extends Cedar with temporal conditions that read an agent's own session event history — a `when temporal { ... }` block with `formerly`, `count_within`, `count_distinct_within`, `sum_within` — and lowers to plain Cedar. Its framing sentence, 'your AI agent's next tool call may be valid but wrong', is the same observation as this repo's 'none of them is an authorization failure; in each case the actor was permitted to do what it did'.

WHERE IT FITS: `dogwood replay policy.dw --policy-schema schema.cedarschema --trace events.log` is exactly the promotion gate docs/work-scoped-governance.md specifies and this repo never built. The temporal operators also express work-item containment natively (formerly = edit only what this item touched; count_within = throttle).

WHY NOT AS THE ENFORCEMENT ENGINE:
1. docs/design/paper.md sec 1 states 'a policy is never DEFINED in yupana' — authoring, SHACL validation and verdict signing stay in quipu. Adopting Dogwood as the authoring language breaks that or adds a second authoring surface.
2. Its own README: it 'accepts timestamps as provided and does not validate them', has 'no authentication mechanism for events', and field inconsistencies SILENTLY WEAKEN CHECKS. AWS says the reference interpreter is not for production. A system founded on three silent-failure incidents cannot put that on the enforcement path.
3. Evidence locality: yupana's evidence is the call graph, blast radius and tenant overlay, none expressible in Cedar's attribute model without shipping the graph into context. Dogwood's escape hatch is a Rhai provider doing an HTTP call per evaluation with 'NO host or IP validation' — against a 100ms deadline.

ACTION: use it OFFLINE only, over the spool, to measure candidate-rule false-positive rates before promotion. Offline is where 'not production-ready' is acceptable. Blocked on the spool carrying session + item (see that bead). Revisit Cedar proper when the declared rung lands, which is when an analyzable authoring language starts paying for itself.
notes: No Cedar or Dogwood reference exists anywhere in quipu, yupana, bobbin or camayoc today — this is a genuinely open choice, recorded so it is not re-litigated from scratch.
close_reason: Built, offline, as scripts/spool-to-dogwood.py plus docs/book/src/reference/replay.md. The assessment in this bead stands unchanged — Dogwood is not adopted as an enforcement engine, because its own README says the reference interpreter is not for production and names silent check-weakening on field mismatch, which is this estate's founding failure class; and because a policy is never DEFINED in yupana. What it IS is the replay runner work-scoped-governance specified and nobody built. The converter's discipline is the denominator: it reports what it dropped with a separate count per reason, since 'no session' and 'resolver abstained' need opposite responses and a single skipped number would hide which is happening. Guard-state kinds are not replayed as actions — that would invent traffic and inflate the very denominator a false-positive rate is measured against. Its tests run inside just test.

title: bobbin: inject-context drops files and tells stderr, so the model reads a truncated block as complete
description:
Two places silently shrink an injection from the model's point of view:

1. src/cli/hook.rs:1410-1427 — the max-chunks cap truncates trailing files and reports with `eprintln!("bobbin: chunks cap dropped {} trailing files ({} chunks > {})")`. A hook's stderr is not injected; the model never sees it.
2. src/cli/hook.rs:1796 and :1876 — the line budget stops emitting chunks mid-list with no marker at all.

The header envelope (src/cli/hook.rs:1574-1607) already carries the right shape — files, direct, coupled, bridged, chunks, budget, injection_id — so the census exists; it just never says what was WITHHELD. An agent reading `<bobbin-context files="6" ...>` has no way to know 14 more files were dropped, and will reasonably treat the block as the answer.

FIX: add `omitted` (and, where the two causes differ, which cause) to the header in all three format modes — xml, minimal, and the default prose line. Keep the stderr line; it is useful to operators.

WHY THIS FRAMING: the same defect exists in quipu (src/context/mod.rs truncates with no counter) and yupana (its advise-mode advisory goes to systemMessage, which the model cannot read). All three report omission to a channel the model cannot see. The estate already states the rule — camayoc's envelope rule (docs/patents/provisional-grounding-cluster.md sec 7: the tier rides the response envelope so an empty answer still declares the tier at which nothing was found) and quipu's own `truncated: {shown, of}` at src/graph_view.rs:239-245.

ACCEPTANCE: an injection that trips either limit reports a non-zero omitted; one that trips neither reports zero (not absent — a missing field reads as 'nothing was dropped' only by luck).
notes: Found 2026-08-18 while planning progressive disclosure across quipu/yupana/bobbin.
close_reason: Done. omitted_files rides ContextSummaryOutput and appears in all three header formats; the line-budget stop, which previously just ended the output, now returns the files it never rendered and the caller writes an explicit marker at the point of the cut. The marker rather than the header because the header is written before any chunk and cannot know.

title: bobbin: give injection_id a retrieval — `bobbin hook expand --injection <id>`
description:
injection_id already exists end to end: it is minted per injection, printed in the context header (src/cli/hook.rs:1574-1607), stored with the injection's files and budget (src/http/client.rs:836-860 store_injection_with_output), and accepted back by the feedback endpoint (src/http/handlers/feedback.rs). It is a handle with no way to redeem it.

FIX: `bobbin hook expand --injection <id> [--limit N]` (plus the matching MCP tool) returning the next slice of what that injection dropped — the files the chunks cap or the line budget cut. This is the pull half of progressive disclosure for CODE context, mirroring the quipu_ask ladder for GRAPH context.

DEPENDS ON the omitted-count bead: an expand call is only trustworthy if the census that advertised it is honest about how much there is.

ACCEPTANCE: expand over an injection that dropped N files returns those files and not the ones already injected; expand over an injection that dropped nothing says so rather than re-serving; an unknown or evicted injection_id is a typed non-answer, never an empty success.
notes: The storage side already retains what is needed; this is a read path, not new retention.
close_reason: Done: bobbin hook expand --injection <id>. No schema change — the stored injection already holds the candidate list and the rendered block, so the withheld set is their difference, which means an injection made before the command existed is still expandable and there is no second record of what was dropped to disagree with the first. Three honesty properties, each tested: an injection that held nothing back SAYS so rather than printing nothing (silence is indistinguishable from a failed lookup); an unreachable server is an error, not an empty answer; and the expansion has a budget of its own and says when it truncates, or it would reintroduce one level down the defect it exists to fix.

title: bobbin: inject-context is work-item-blind, so retrieval restarts from zero every prompt
description:
yupana/docs/work-scoped-governance.md sec 3 names this exactly: 'Semantic-search context injection already exists as a prompt-submit hook, but it is work-item-blind: it sees the prompt text and nothing about what the agent is actually assigned to.'

The consequence it names is the interesting one: 'agents rediscover the same context repeatedly because retrieval is per-prompt and stateless. Keyed on the work item, retrieval becomes cumulative — the second session on an item starts where the first finished.'

FIX: read the plate — $SHANTY_ROOT/crew/$SHANTY_AGENT/plate.json, the same small file yupana/src/plate.rs reads and shantytown/shantytown/plate_publish.py writes — and key retrieval on the work item alongside the prompt text.

READ THE FILE, DO NOT CALL YUPANA. yupana/src/brief.rs:19-26 sets the division of labour: bobbin owns SEMANTIC CODE context, yupana's briefing owns GOVERNANCE/WORK-ITEM context, and neither shells out to the other because nesting one tool's injection inside the other's injects the same context twice. Both reading one published file is precisely why plate_publish exists.

ABSTAIN, NEVER GUESS: missing, malformed or stale plate means UNKNOWN — fall back to today's prompt-only behaviour. Do not invent a work item.

ACCEPTANCE: with a plate present, two sessions on the same item do not re-inject identical context; with no plate, behaviour is byte-identical to today.
notes: Also the precondition for deriving relevance labels from what an agent actually edited after being briefed.
close_reason: Done via src/plate.rs, reading the same published file yupana reads — no call to yupana, which would nest one tool's injection inside the other's. The item is APPENDED to the query, never substituted: the prompt stays the dominant signal. An unknown plate leaves the query byte-identical to before, because a wrong work item would skew every retrieval in a session while looking exactly like it was working.

title: bobbin: `cargo fmt` pushes two files past the size ratchet, and nothing gates fmt
description:
FOUND 2026-08-18 while implementing the plate-aware injection. Running `cargo fmt` on a clean tree reformats a large part of the repo — it is not fmt-clean — and two of the resulting files land over the hard file-size limit:

  src/http/handlers/search.rs  492 -> 502 lines (limit 500)
  src/search/intent.rs         ~   -> 526 lines (limit 500)

So `cargo fmt` followed by `just check` is red, while `just check` alone is green. That is a trap with a sharp edge: `just check` does NOT run `cargo fmt --check` (unlike quipu and yupana, which both do), so nothing tells a contributor the tree is unformatted, and the first person to run the formatter as a courtesy breaks the gate in two files they never touched.

TWO WAYS FORWARD, and they are not equivalent:

1. Format the tree once, split the two files that go over, and add `cargo fmt --check` to the pre-commit config — bringing bobbin in line with its sibling repos. This is the honest one: the ratchet exists to force extraction, and two files being over after formatting means they were already too big and whitespace was hiding it.
2. Leave it, and accept that `cargo fmt` is effectively forbidden here. If this is the choice, it should be WRITTEN DOWN, because right now the only way to discover it is to run the formatter and watch an unrelated gate fail.

Not fixed in the pass that found it: reformatting the tree would have buried a behaviour change under a few thousand lines of whitespace diff, and the split it forces is a real refactor rather than a mechanical one.
notes: Discovered by doing it: `cargo fmt` was run reflexively, blew the ratchet, and was reverted so the commit stayed scoped. The revert is why this is a bead and not a diff.
close_reason: Fixed the honest way rather than by writing down the trap. The tree is formatted, the two files that then went over the hard limit are split by ROLE — intent.rs keeps 'what is this query' and hands the tuning table to intent_adjustments.rs; search.rs keeps request shaping and response assembly and hands the two executors to search_exec.rs — and `cargo fmt --check` is now a pre-commit hook, which is what quipu and yupana both had and bobbin did not. That absence is why the drift accumulated silently: nothing told a contributor the tree was unformatted, so the first person to run the formatter as a courtesy broke a gate in two files they never opened. Both files being over after formatting is the ratchet's point — they were already too big and whitespace was hiding it. just check and cargo test are green (968 + 82).

title: shantytown: a permissions test cannot fail when the suite runs as root
description:
FOUND 2026-08-18. `tests/test_plate_publish.py::test_publish_never_raises_on_an_unwritable_root` creates a directory, chmods it 0o500, and asserts `publish(...) is False` — i.e. that the write was refused. Root ignores permission bits, so the write SUCCEEDS, `publish` returns True, and the test fails. It fails on a completely clean tree; it has nothing to do with any change.

The fix is not to delete it. What it asserts is genuinely load-bearing — publishing is bookkeeping alongside a command the operator actually asked for, and a full disk or a read-only root must never turn `st anchor` into a traceback. The problem is the MECHANISM: a permission bit is not a way to make a write fail for uid 0, so under root the test is not lenient, it is VACUOUS — it exercises the success path while claiming to exercise the failure path, and its green result under a normal uid says nothing about whether it would still catch a regression under CI's.

Options: skip explicitly when `os.geteuid() == 0`, with the skip reason naming why (an honest 'not measured here' beats a false pass); or induce the failure by a means root respects — an unwritable path component, a nonexistent parent, or monkeypatching the write to raise. The second keeps the coverage; the first at least stops the suite lying about having it.

Either way the current state is the shape this repo refuses everywhere else: a check that cannot fail in the environment it runs in.
notes: Not fixed in the pass that found it — it is unrelated to the containment work and deserves its own decision about which mechanism replaces the chmod. Pre-existing: reproduced on a stashed clean tree.
close_reason: Fixed. The chmod mechanism is replaced with a regular FILE in the path, which no uid can mkdir through, so the assertion holds for root and non-root alike; the chmod case is kept but explicitly SKIPPED under root, because an honest 'not measured here' beats a pass that means nothing. A control asserts the same call returns True when the tree is creatable — without it the replacement could have stopped working and still looked green. shantytown's suite is now fully green: 2282 passed, 0 failed.

title: yupana: FR-40 blessed-path projection - a path rule plane over the existing quipu projection
description: yupana docs/golden-path-guard.md FR-40 (design intent, nothing built). Project L3+ golden paths from quipu over the existing policy-projection path (src/hook/rule_planes.rs) into a NEW rule plane keyed by the tenant's declared followsPath, not by selector match. Each projected path carries its blessing level, conformance grammar version (quipu-gp1), and exemplar citations. Projection freshness served on every conformance verdict, as rule verdicts do today. title: Surface tripwire policies in agent context (governed Binding/Gate)
description: The stack now has TRIPWIRES: path-boundary policies bound to an effect (warn/deny/throttle). Locally in yupana ([[yupana.policy.tripwires]], yupana main b740ea4) and governed in quipu (aegis:Policy at boundary "action" with aegis:appliesTo and no Selector/Predicate — quipu shapes/policies/tripwire.ttl, main 0ae7e88; projected+enforced by yupana main 9b736fa). Bobbin's role (governance-plane design: authoring intelligence + surfacing) suggests two slices: (1) surface active tripwire boundaries in injected context so an agent learns a wire exists BEFORE tripping it — the session-start briefing precedent; (2) conversational authoring of a wire from a natural-language boundary description, written to quipu as the governed form. Evidence: yupana docs/book/src/reference/policy-guard.md#tripwires--boundaries-with-declared-effects.
notes:
Implemented (2026-08-25). Bobbin's half of the pitch — slice (1), surfacing — is built; slice (2), conversational authoring of a wire into quipu, is NOT and stays open as a separate concern.

WHAT SHIPPED
- New module src/tripwire/{mod,decode,render,cache,tests}.rs. Projects quipu's tripwire policies (aegis:Policy at boundary "action" with aegis:appliesTo and no selector/predicate) over the EXISTING quipu_endpoint key via POST /query, and prepends a governed-boundary section to injected context naming the wires that span the files in the bundle.
- Wired into BOTH injection paths at once (the bobbin-dee condition): inject_context_inner (local) and inject_context_remote (thin client) both call crate::tripwire::with_boundaries. Deliberately NOT routed through the /context response — see below.
- Docs: docs/book/src/guides/governed-boundaries.md (+ SUMMARY, cross-links from quipu-integration.md and hooks.md).
- 27 unit tests.

DESIGN DECISIONS worth reviewing
1. Client-side in both paths, not server-side. Putting the wires on /context would keep the thin client thin, but it would make 'which boundaries am I told about' depend on which bobbin deployment answered — exactly the divergence that deferred bobbin-dee — and would let a search host suppress a governance boundary. Cost: a thin client must reach quipu itself. It already loads local bobbin config for every other hook setting.
2. No new config keys. quipu_endpoint (+ BOBBIN_QUIPU_REMOTE) is the transport, matching src/mcp/server.rs's argument against a second knob meaning the same thing. No endpoint => no HTTP call, no section, no hot-path cost. (Also forced: src/config.rs is at its file-size ceiling.)
3. Bobbin never DROPS a wire it cannot understand. Yupana refuses a projection carrying an unenforceable effect, correctly — a dropped wire there reads as guarded and is not. Here the failure inverts: a dropped wire is a boundary nobody is warned about. So an unrecognised effect (require-approval, escalate, record, allow) is surfaced verbatim, an absent one is surfaced as undeclared, and a conflicting-rows policy is marked conflicted rather than resolved by row order or voiding the batch.
4. Every rendered line is a declaration, never a promise. The section says outright that bobbin does not enforce. Bobbin has no pre-edit hook.
5. Freshness is stated, not assumed. .bobbin/tripwire-cache.json, 300s TTL, 2s timeout (matching the spotlight call). A failed refresh serves last-known wires and SAYS the refresh failed; with zero matches AND a failed refresh the section still appears saying only that, because 'I could not look' is not 'there was nothing'.

MISSING UPSTREAM — worth a quipu bead
aegis:appliesTo globs are repo-relative and carry NO repo/module scoping. Yupana is per-tenant so this never arises there; bobbin indexes many repos, so 'src/auth/**' matches that relative path in every indexed repo. Bobbin does not guess: it names the repo per matched path and adds a caveat line when matches span >1 repo. A proper fix needs a repo/module scoping term in shapes/policies/tripwire.ttl.

NOT PROVEN END TO END: there is no quipu server in this environment, so the HTTP transport is untested against a live endpoint. Decode, matching, staleness accounting and rendering are unit-tested; the query text is held in step with yupana's by an assertion, not by a live round trip.

title: Spec then build parenthesised/nested boolean query grouping
description:
The last remaining half of GitHub #50 (now closed; its three numbered items shipped 2026-08-25).

`(redis OR memcached) AND cache` mis-tokenises into the literal words `(redis` and `memcached)`. `src/search/query.rs` has no recursive AST — it uses flat `Vec`s plus a `has_or` flag, and `split_on_or` is a flat string operation over " OR ". The design in docs/plans/advanced-query-syntax.md sketches a `Term { Word, Phrase, Not, And, Or, Regex }` tree that was never built.

Deliberately NOT attempted in the #50 sweep: grouped-boolean semantics need writing down first. Open questions the spec must answer before any parser work:
- How do inline filters interact with grouping? `(repo:a OR repo:b) foo` is a filter disjunction, which `filters_to_sql` cannot currently express (it ANDs clauses).
- What does a grouped branch mean for the OR execution strategy, which today runs each branch as a separate index query and merges by best score? Nested groups multiply branches.
- Does NOT distribute over a group, and is `-(a OR b)` accepted?
- Precedence and associativity, since today's flat split has neither.

Acceptance: a written grouping spec merged into docs/plans/advanced-query-syntax.md; THEN a recursive-descent parser producing the Term tree plus an execution planner; both surfaces (HTTP /search and `bobbin search`) get it for free because both call query::parse and query::retain_matching.

Note also unverified-in-CI gap: bobbin search's result-returning path was exercised only by unit tests during the #50 work, because the sweep environment could not download the ONNX embedding model. tests/cli_search.rs self-skips on that condition — worth confirming those integration tests actually run somewhere.
notes:
Spec half DONE (2026-08-25). Build remains OPEN, pending review of the eight questions the spec raises.

SPEC: docs/designs/query-grouping.md. Cross-linked from docs/plans/advanced-query-syntax.md (status banner + Phase 3), which it supersedes for the Term-enum sketch — that sketch predates the flat parser that actually shipped.

Deviation from this bead's acceptance wording, recorded deliberately: the bead said 'merged into docs/plans/advanced-query-syntax.md'. It is a standalone design doc instead, because that plan carries an implementation-status banner describing SHIPPED work, and folding ~350 lines of unbuilt grammar into it would make the banner lie about what exists. The plan links to it from both places a reader would look. Convention followed is docs/designs/context-bundles.md — a design doc with a status banner.

COVERS, as required: the grammar (EBNF) with a precedence table; composition with each of the four features that shipped in the #50 sweep (+required, negation, regex, field filters incl. repo:/group:); the parsed response field's shape; migration for currently-valid flat queries; and the SQL-vs-in-memory execution split.

The load-bearing findings:
- filters_to_sql returning Vec<String> that every caller ANDs IS the reason (repo:a OR repo:b) cannot be expressed. It has to return one parenthesised expression built from the tree. group:'s current special-casing (excluded from filters_to_sql, handled by the caller) must move INTO the SQL builder, because the caller no longer sees a flat list to intercept. That is the single largest mechanical change in the build.
- The one real migration break is 'fn foo()' — a bare paren in an ordinary code search. Proposed fix: parens are grouping tokens only in a primary position, so 'fn foo()' is unchanged. This makes the lexer position-sensitive, which it is not today.
- has_or == true currently IMPLIES or_branches.len() > 1, and both executors branch on exactly that conjunction. A NESTED or breaks the implication. Recommendation: add has_nested_or rather than redefine has_or, so a shipped contract stays literally true.
- Naive lowering of nested ORs is a cross product of full searches — (a OR b) AND (c OR d) is four, three levels is eight, and a user can write that in twenty characters. Spec proposes: DNF for the SQL predicate only; split retrieval on OR only where branches carry DIFFERENT text queries; cap retrieval branches at 8 and ANNOUNCE the fallback in the response.
- De Morgan on -(a OR b) is standard and recommended, but -(a AND b) becomes a disjunction of negations, which is not expressible as today's cheap 'drop results containing X' post-filter. Nested negation cannot be bolted onto the existing executor.
- Mixed-plane negation, -(redis OR repo:aegis), straddles SQL and in-memory. The planner must run De Morgan BEFORE the SQL/in-memory partition, not after.
- Acceptance criteria include writing the golden-file regression suite against the CURRENT parser first, so 'same results as before' is executable rather than asserted.

EIGHT OPEN QUESTIONS for Stiwi are tabulated in §9 with a recommendation for each. Two of them (#3 mixed-plane negation, #6 full-scan for a balanced closer) change what EXISTING queries do; the other six only affect what new queries can express.

Also recorded, not fixed: this bead's own note about tests/cli_search.rs self-skipping when the ONNX model cannot be downloaded is real and wants its own bead — a grouping suite that self-skips proves nothing. There is no route to huggingface.co in this environment, so that gap could not be closed here either.
