title: Beads-specific relevance gate for hook context injection (GH#52 Phase 3)
description:
Named in GH#52 as the "smaller companion gap (Phase 3)" and in
docs/plans/beads-integration.md Phase 3: "Gate by relevance threshold (avoid
noise)". Filed rather than implemented alongside index-bead because it is a
policy change needing threshold/cap values Stiwi should set, and because the
obvious insertion points are both inside large files.

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY
Bead chunks reach injected context through the GENERIC path — they compete for
the same budget as source chunks, under the same gate, with no dedicated
threshold and no cap. `grep -n 'ChunkType::Issue' src/cli/hook.rs` returns
nothing.

WHY THAT IS A GAP, NOT JUST AN OMISSION
A bead is prose about work, so it embeds closer to a natural-language prompt
than source code does. Under one shared gate the beads win ties they should
lose, and a prompt that wants code gets issue text. The plan's "avoid noise" is
naming exactly this.

WHERE IT WOULD GO (surveyed 2026-08-25, do not take on trust)
Bead chunks are identifiable by key prefix with no new field: `file_path`
starts with `beads:` (src/index/beads/keys.rs::bead_file_path). There are TWO
injection paths and they do not share a filter point:
  - remote/thin-client: src/cli/hook.rs ~1690-1765 gates `resp_files` and then
    applies a hardcoded 12-chunk cap.
  - local: assembles a `ContextBundle` (src/search/context.rs) and formats via
    `format_context_for_injection` (src/cli/hook.rs:2644).
Gating in ONE of the two is worse than gating in neither — it makes behaviour
depend on whether the hook is thin-client or local, which nothing else does.
The likely right seam is bundle assembly in src/search/context.rs, which the
HTTP /context endpoint also goes through, so the remote path inherits it. That
needs checking, not assuming.

ACCEPTANCE
- One config knob pair under [hooks] (a beads gate threshold and a max beads
  file count), defaulted so current behaviour is a deliberate choice rather
  than an accident.
- The gate applies identically whether the hook runs local or thin-client, with
  a test that asserts the two agree.
- A test that a low-scoring bead is excluded while a same-scoring source chunk
  is kept.
- Docs: docs/book/src/guides/hooks.md and the config reference.

NOTE ON FILE SIZE
src/cli/hook.rs is ~9,878 lines and src/search/context.rs ~3,149; both are
allowlisted. Since the allowlist froze per-file ceilings, neither may grow — so
this work carries a split with it, not just an insertion.

title: Batch the chunks-table schema migration (occurred_at + source discriminator + W1.P3 identity)
description:
SPEC ONLY — DO NOT START. This needs Stiwi's sign-off on TIMING before any code
lands, because executing it re-embeds every chunk in every deployed store. It is
filed so the queue exists, not so someone picks it up.

## Why this is one batched event and not three changes

`VectorStore::open_with_dim` (src/storage/lance.rs:296-352) compares the on-disk
chunks-table field list against `build_schema` and, on ANY difference, calls
`conn.drop_table(TABLE_NAME)`:

    if on_disk != expected_fields {
        eprintln!("bobbin: chunks table schema changed — dropping for re-creation");
        conn.drop_table(TABLE_NAME, &[]).await?;

So adding ONE column silently destroys the corpus and forces a full re-index and
re-embed of every repo in the store. Not a migration — a drop with a stderr line
that a cron job's output nobody reads.

That makes the first column addition a one-time event with a real cost, and
every other pending chunks-table change should ride along with it rather than
paying that cost again. `docs/plans/bobbin-roadmap.md:189-192` states this
directly ("this lands as ONE batched migration event ... with explicit operator
comms, not as drive-by columns") and :59 makes it the gate: "the `occurred_at`
chunks-table migration gates W4.P3 and should absorb every other pending
chunks-table change."

## Current schema (measured, `build_schema`)

id, vector, repo, file_path, file_hash, language, chunk_type, chunk_name,
start_line, end_line, content, full_context, indexed_at, tags

## What must batch together

1. **`occurred_at`** — event time. Gates W4.P3 (logs + metrics), which is the
   last unshipped item in W4; W4.P1/P2 are done. Roadmap :188-196, listed `open`
   in the cross-repo register at :241. Zero hits in src/ today.

2. **A real `source` discriminator.** Roadmap :194 asks for "a `source` column,
   not more `file_path` pseudo-namespaces" — and the situation is worse than
   that line suggests. `VectorStore::insert`'s fifth parameter is `file_hash`
   (src/storage/lance.rs:621-628), and `index_hashed_source` /
   `index_watermark_source` pass `source.source_label()` into it
   (src/index/source.rs:134 and :230). The source label for beads, SQL, archive
   and commit rows is therefore stored in the file_hash COLUMN. Meanwhile the
   corpus is separated by `file_path` prefixes (`beads:{rig}:{id}`) and by
   synthetic repo keys (`beads-issues`, `archive-records`). Three overloaded
   fields doing one column's job.

3. **Any W1.P3 identity promotion.** Roadmap :86-94. Chunk ids are
   `sha256(path:start:end)`, so any line shift re-mints them; stable
   ordinal-based identity is wanted "when dangling rates annoy". If it is going
   to happen it costs nothing extra inside this batch and a second full re-embed
   outside it. NOTE the `repo` column on **chunk_edges** is NOT part of this
   batch: that is an edges-only drop, edges rebuild on force reindex with no
   re-embed, so it is cheap and independent — do not couple it in.

Before executing, re-scan for anything else queued behind a chunks-table
change; this list is what was pending on 2026-08-25, not a closed set.

## Operator comms — a required deliverable, not a courtesy

The drop is silent by design today and the migration must not be. Specify and
ship, in the same change:

- A CHANGELOG entry naming the re-embed and its cost per store size.
- A pre-flight refusal: on detecting a schema difference, `bobbin index` should
  REQUIRE an explicit acknowledgement flag rather than dropping and continuing.
  A gate that only warns is the same failure as the one being fixed.
- `bobbin status` should report the schema version it is running against so an
  operator can tell before running anything whether their store will be dropped.
- A stated re-embed duration estimate from a measured store, not an assumed one.

## Acceptance

- All three changes land in one commit; the chunks table is dropped exactly
  once.
- `bobbin index` refuses to drop the table without an explicit acknowledgement.
- `bobbin status` reports schema version, and the CHANGELOG names the cost.
- `source_label` writes to the new `source` column; nothing writes a source
  label into `file_hash` (add a test — the current overload is invisible and
  will otherwise be re-added).
- The synthetic `beads-issues` / `archive-records` repo keys are reviewed
  against the new column; keep them only if they still earn their place.

## Blocked on

Stiwi's decision on WHEN. Not on any technical dependency.

title: tests/cli_search.rs self-skips without the ONNX model — the CLI search path is unverified in CI
description:
Split out of bobbin-0a5's closing note, because a grouping test suite that self-skips proves nothing and the same is already true of the suite that exists.

tests/cli_search.rs self-skips when the ONNX embedding model cannot be downloaded. During the GH#50 sweep that condition held, so `bobbin search`'s result-returning path was exercised only by unit tests — no integration test was ever OBSERVED to run it. A test that silently passes by not running is indistinguishable from one that passed, which is the defect class this repo keeps writing comments about.

Acceptance:
- Determine whether these tests run anywhere (CI with a model cache? a nightly?). If they do, say where, in a comment in the test file, so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.
- If they do not, make the skip LOUD rather than silent — a skipped integration test should be visible in the run summary, not a green line.
- Ideally: a checked-in tiny fixture model or a recorded-embedding fake so the CLI result path is exercised without network. Note that the environments where this keeps biting have no route to huggingface.co.

Filed by strider, 2026-08-25, alongside the bobbin-0a5 spec.

title: upstream (quipu): aegis:appliesTo has no repo/module scoping, so a tripwire matches every indexed repo
description:
Found while implementing bobbin-0d9. Needs a decision in quipu, not bobbin; filed here so bobbin's workaround has something to point at.

quipu's tripwire shape (shapes/policies/tripwire.ttl) scopes a policy with aegis:appliesTo, documented in docs/book/src/concepts/governance.md as 'repo-relative path globs'. There is no term saying WHICH repo. That is fine for yupana, which is per-tenant and therefore has exactly one; it is not fine for bobbin, which indexes many repos in one table. A wire declared 'src/auth/**' matches that relative path in aegis, bobbin, quipu and every other indexed repo alike.

Bobbin does not guess. src/tripwire/render.rs names the repo alongside each matched path (aegis:src/auth/login.rs) and, when matches span more than one repo, emits a line saying the globs carry no repo scoping so the reader can judge which matches were meant. That is honest but it is a caveat, not a fix.

A fix wants a scoping term on the policy — a repo/module/tenant predicate that aegis:appliesTo is read relative to — plus a rule for what an unscoped wire means (all repos? refuse?). Note the shape already carries aegis:targets "CodeModule", which is a TYPE and not an instance, so it does not answer this.

Filed by strider, 2026-08-25. Escalate to whoever owns camayoc/quipu ontology.

title: Bump the quipu pin from 0.3.23 to 0.3.26
description:
Cargo.toml pins quipu by rev 37bfc06a = 0.3.23 (current main as of 2026-08-22). quipu has since released 0.3.26, and the pin comment's own rationale — pinned by rev so the compiled quipu cannot drift from the rev this code was adapted to — is why this needs a deliberate bump rather than a floating dep.

Newly available since 0.3.23: [[quipu.attachments]] config mounting declared layers at open (plus quipu db attach --list); declared trust labels at the federation edge, so [quipu.labels] floors gate federated reads; quipu audit namespace (report-only listing of episode-minted predicates no shape mentions); freeze/archive packs now carry entity embeddings, with thaw and graph import restoring them; agent transition signatures verified at the write gate; the placement rule that a throttle effect must declare a backoffFormula; pack --space to ship a pack in a designated term space.

KNOWN BREAKING CHANGE, verify before bumping: provider::federated_from_config now returns Result rather than the bare value (it can refuse a malformed remote label declaration). Any bobbin caller compiled against the old signature will fail to build. Check the knowledge feature's call sites.

Also worth checking during the bump: quipu 0.3.26 wires vector.backend to actually select the LanceDB backend in-binary when the feature is compiled, and makes the key a HARD ERROR when the feature is absent rather than a silent SQLite fallback — if bobbin sets that key anywhere, the failure mode changed.

Precedent: bobbin-c58 was the 0.3.23 bump and is the shape to follow. Requires a full build plus the knowledge-feature test pass; this container has no route to huggingface.co so an end-to-end index cannot be proven here.

title: Optional cross-encoder reranking stage for hybrid search

title: Generic documents source: HTML text extraction through the hashed-source lifecycle
description: Gap G3 from caboodle docs/design/txtai-gap-analysis.md. Non-code surface today is markdown + opt-in PDF text; no generic document loader. Add a documents source (start: .html/.htm to text/markdown-ish, deterministic, no model in the loop) reusing ChunkSource + index_hashed_source and the existing chunkers. Acceptance: html files indexed and searchable; incremental re-index skips unchanged; parse failure degrades to skip with warning, never a crash.
close_reason: Shipped in a6482d7: [index] documents=true (default off, mirrors multimodal opt-in) walks **/*.html|htm, converts via a deterministic dependency-free tag stripper (script/style/head/comments dropped, headings->markdown #, li->bullets, pre->fences, entities decoded), feeds the existing markdown chunker so headings become breadcrumb section chunks tagged language=html. No new dependency (checked cargo tree: no suitable HTML parser present; quick-xml transitive only). Failure posture matches multimodal: extraction error -> per-file warning+skip, empty text -> skip. Incremental re-index skips unchanged files via the existing content-hash path (covered by index_incremental_skips_unchanged_files; extraction runs upstream of hashing). Tests: 16 documents unit/pipeline tests + collect_files/read_indexable_content gating. Docs: config/index.md Documents source section next to the PDF one.

title: Persist similar_to chunk edges from the near-duplicate scan
description: Gap G5 from caboodle docs/design/txtai-gap-analysis.md. bobbin similar --scan already clusters near-duplicates and discards the edges. Persist them as similar_to rows in chunk_edges (threshold-gated, opt-in) so context assembly gains a semantic-neighbor leg; where the knowledge feature is on, mint as quarantined low-trust facts, never as observation. Acceptance: opt-in flag writes edges idempotently; edges queryable via chunk_neighbors; documented.
close_reason: Shipped in 2046e21: similar --scan --persist writes threshold-gated pairs as similar_to edges in chunk_edges (new ChunkEdgeType::SimilarTo). Idempotent replace-on-persist within repo scope via clear_chunk_edges_by_type; direction normalized (smaller chunk ID first). Queryable through chunk_neighbors MCP/HTTP like other edge types; edge_type filter accepts similar_to. Unit tests: normalization, idempotent re-run, shrink/empty re-persist, repo-scoped replace, threshold gating, scan+persist roundtrip. Docs: cli/similar.md + mcp/tools.md. Deferred: quipu/knowledge lane (quarantined low-trust facts) — bead scopes it to knowledge-enabled setups; follow-up work.
